Synopsis:
    Fitch's upgrade of Portugal's debt is the latest in a series of credit rating improvements among former PIIGS nations, marking a structural reversal since the 2011 euro zone debt crisis. While Portugal, Ireland, Greece and Spain have meaningfully reduced debt burdens and regained credit standing, Italy remains the outlier with stagnant growth and a rising debt-to-GDP ratio set to surpass Greece as the most indebted euro zone country. Pressure has shifted toward Germany, where AfD electoral gains and fiscal questions are pushing Bund yields to their highest since 2011, and France, both previously considered the bloc's safe anchors.
